result:
Signed-in users can now comment on posts, delete comments they're allowed to delete, and report comments. A comment disappears from the post page once three different users have reported it. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (8 tests across 3 files) and `bunx guren gate` all pass. I didn't boot the app, so the new comment section on the post page hasn't been checked in a browser.

**Behaviour:**
- **Guests** posting, deleting or reporting get the same redirect to `/login` as the rest of the app.
- **Comments** must be 1–2000 characters. Anything else fails with the same 422 an invalid post title gives, and nothing is stored. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed first, the same way titles are, so a body of only spaces counts as empty.
- **Deleting** works for the comment's author or the post's author and redirects to the post; anyone else gets 403. It removes the comment's reports too.
- **Reporting** always answers 204. A repeat report by the same user still leaves one row.
- **Post page** lists visible comments oldest first as `{ id, body, author: { id, name }, createdAt }`. Hidden comments are left out for everyone but stay in the `comments` table.
- **Deleting a post** removes its comments and their reports.

**Decision for you:** the existing Show page decides who sees Edit/Delete by reading a signed-in user the server never sends, so it always comes out empty. I passed a new `viewerId` prop instead, and the comment controls and the post's Edit/Delete buttons use it. That means Edit/Delete on your own post now actually appear. I kept `viewerId` separate so each comment's props stay exactly the shape in the contract.

I added tables `comments` and `comment_reports` in `db/schema.ts` (with a unique index on `comment_id`, `user_id`) and a migration in `db/migrations/20260929144449_add_comments`. The new code is the `Comment` and `CommentReport` models, `CommentPolicy` (registered in `AuthorizationProvider`), `CommentValidator`, `CommentResource` and `CommentController`. Its routes are in `routes/web.ts`: `comments.store` behind the existing login check under `/posts`, and `comments.destroy` and `comments.report` under `/comments`. `PostController.show` now passes `comments` and `viewerId`, and `destroy` removes the post's comments and reports in code, because the database's own cascade only works in SQLite when a setting is turned on. `resources/js/pages/posts/Show.tsx` shows the comment list, a comment box when signed in, and Delete/Report buttons. New tests in `tests/CommentController.test.ts` cover every case in the acceptance list.
